test_cases.test_name: Verify Continuous Temperature Monitoring and Data Recording Intervals
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS continuously monitors temperature in GMP storage areas and records readings at intervals not exceeding 5 minutes.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Temperature sensors are installed and calibrated in all GMP storage areas.
Access to EMS software interface and data logs.

test_steps.action: Observe the EMS interface for a continuous period of at least 10 minutes in a designated GMP storage area.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS interface displays real-time temperature readings for the monitored area without interruption.
data_to_capture: Screenshots of EMS interface showing continuous monitoring.

test_steps.action: Access the recorded data logs for the same GMP storage area during the observation period.
test_steps.expected_result: Temperature readings are recorded at intervals of 5 minutes or less, with timestamps for each reading.
data_to_capture: Exported data log file showing temperature readings and timestamps.

acceptance_criteria: Continuous temperature monitoring is visually confirmed.
All recorded temperature data points are within 5-minute intervals.
data_integrity_requirements: Data is recorded accurately and without loss.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Temperature Range, Accuracy, and Alarm Deviation
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS operates within the specified temperature range, maintains accuracy, and generates alerts when temperature deviates from the setpoint.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Calibrated temperature probes are installed in GMP storage areas.
Access to EMS software interface and alarm configuration.
Reference calibrated thermometer for verification.

test_steps.action: Set a target temperature within the EMS for a specific GMP storage area (e.g., 20°C).
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS accepts the setpoint and displays it correctly.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of EMS interface showing the setpoint.

test_steps.action: Using a calibrated reference thermometer, introduce a temperature change in the monitored area to simulate a deviation of +2°C from the setpoint (e.g., 22°C).
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS detects the temperature increase and generates an alert within 30 seconds.
data_to_capture: Screenshots of EMS interface showing the elevated temperature and active alarm.

test_steps.action: Introduce a temperature change to simulate a deviation of -2°C from the setpoint (e.g., 18°C).
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS detects the temperature decrease and generates an alert within 30 seconds.
data_to_capture: Screenshots of EMS interface showing the decreased temperature and active alarm.

test_steps.action: Verify the accuracy of the EMS reading against the reference thermometer when the temperature is stable within the specified range (e.g., at 20°C).
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS temperature reading is within ±0.5°C of the reference thermometer reading.
data_to_capture: Screenshots of EMS interface showing temperature reading.

acceptance_criteria: The EMS accurately displays setpoints.
Alarms are generated within 30 seconds for +2°C and -2°C deviations.
Temperature readings are accurate within ±0.5°C of the reference thermometer.
data_integrity_requirements: Temperature readings are accurate and reflect actual conditions.
Alarm triggers are reliable and timely.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Vendor Software Unmodified and Data Storage Format
test_cases.objective: To verify that the vendor-supplied software is used without modification and that data is stored in the vendor's standard database format.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Access to system logs and configuration files.

test_steps.action: Review system installation and configuration documentation to confirm no modifications were made to the vendor-supplied software.
test_steps.expected_result: Documentation confirms that the vendor-supplied software has not been modified.

test_steps.action: Generate a sample report or export data from the EMS system.
test_steps.expected_result: The exported data or report is in the vendor's standard database format (e.g., CSV, specific database schema).

acceptance_criteria: The vendor-supplied software is confirmed to be unmodified.
Data is stored and exportable in the vendor's standard database format.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Alarm Notification and Response Time
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system generates alerts when temperature deviates from setpoint and that the system response time for alarm conditions does not exceed 30 seconds.
prerequisites: EMS system is operational and monitoring temperature.
Defined temperature setpoints are configured.
Site paging system is accessible for testing.
Ability to simulate temperature deviations.

test_steps.action: Set a temperature setpoint for a monitored area.
test_steps.expected_result: Setpoint is successfully configured in the EMS.

test_steps.action: Simulate a temperature deviation exceeding the ±2°C alarm threshold (e.g., by temporarily adjusting a local thermostat or using a calibrated temperature simulator).
test_steps.expected_result: An alarm is triggered in the EMS and a notification is sent to the site paging system.

test_steps.action: Measure the time from the simulated temperature deviation to the receipt of the alarm notification on the paging system.
test_steps.expected_result: The response time is less than or equal to 30 seconds.

test_steps.action: Return the simulated temperature to within the acceptable range and verify the alarm clears.
test_steps.expected_result: The alarm status in the EMS is updated to indicate the condition has cleared.

acceptance_criteria: The system generates alerts when temperature deviates ±2°C from setpoint.
Alarm notifications are successfully sent to the site paging system.
System response time for alarm conditions does not exceed 30 seconds.
Alarm status correctly updates when the condition is resolved.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Audit Trail and Electronic Signature Functionality
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system maintains a comprehensive audit trail and supports electronic signatures as per 21 CFR Part 11.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
User accounts with appropriate permissions are created.
A simulated temperature deviation event has occurred.

test_steps.action: Log in to the EMS system with an administrator account.
test_steps.expected_result: Successful login and access to system administration functions.

test_steps.action: Navigate to the audit trail section and filter for the simulated temperature deviation event.
test_steps.expected_result: The audit trail displays all relevant actions related to the event, including user, date, time, and action performed.
data_to_capture: Audit trail log entries for the event

test_steps.action: Attempt to modify a recorded data point or audit trail entry without proper authorization.
test_steps.expected_result: The system prevents modification and logs the unauthorized access attempt in the audit trail.
data_to_capture: Audit trail log entry for the attempted modification

test_steps.action: Initiate an action requiring an electronic signature (e.g., acknowledging an alarm, approving a report).
test_steps.expected_result: The system prompts for electronic signature credentials.

test_steps.action: Provide valid electronic signature credentials and confirm the action.
test_steps.expected_result: The action is successfully completed and electronically signed, with the signature details recorded in the audit trail.
data_to_capture: Electronic signature details (user, date, time, reason)
Audit trail entry for the signed action

acceptance_criteria: All actions performed by users are logged in the audit trail with sufficient detail.
The audit trail is protected from unauthorized modification or deletion.
Electronic signatures are captured accurately and linked to the relevant actions.
The system enforces the use of electronic signatures for critical operations as defined by vendor software.
data_integrity_requirements: Audit trail must be complete, consistent, and accurate.
Electronic signatures must be unique to the individual and securely linked to the signed record.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Data Archival and Storage Capacity
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system can store data for at least 10 years and that the archival process functions correctly.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Sufficient historical data exists to simulate a period of operation.
Vendor documentation for archival process is available.

test_steps.action: Review vendor documentation to understand the data archival process and configuration settings.
test_steps.expected_result: Documentation clearly outlines the steps and parameters for data archival.

test_steps.action: Configure the system's archival settings to meet the 7-year retention requirement (or a shorter period for testing purposes if feasible).
test_steps.expected_result: Archival settings are successfully applied within the system.

test_steps.action: Simulate data generation over a period that would trigger archival (e.g., simulate 1 year of data if archival is set to 1 year).
test_steps.expected_result: The system generates continuous temperature and humidity data.

test_steps.action: Initiate the archival process manually or wait for the scheduled archival to occur.
test_steps.expected_result: The archival process completes successfully without errors.

test_steps.action: Verify that the data older than the archival threshold has been moved to the archive location and is no longer readily accessible in the primary database.
test_steps.expected_result: Archived data is stored in the designated archive location and is not present in the active database.
data_to_capture: Confirmation of data in archive location
Absence of archived data in active database

test_steps.action: Attempt to retrieve archived data using the vendor's specified retrieval method.
test_steps.expected_result: Archived data can be successfully retrieved and is accurate.

test_steps.action: Assess the system's storage capacity by estimating the total data generated over 10 years based on current monitoring frequency and data size.
test_steps.expected_result: The system's storage capacity is sufficient to support 10 years of continuous monitoring.

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully archives data according to the configured retention period.
Archived data is retrievable and remains accurate.
The system's storage capacity is adequate for 10 years of continuous monitoring.
The archival process does not negatively impact system performance.
data_integrity_requirements: Data must be retained for the specified period.
Archived data must be protected from loss or corruption.
Archived data must be retrievable for review and analysis.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Standard Reports for Batch Release
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system generates standard reports as provided by the vendor for use in batch release.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System (EMS) is installed and configured.
Sufficient historical data exists to generate reports.

test_steps.action: Access the reporting module of the EMS.
test_steps.expected_result: The reporting module is accessible and displays available report options.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the reporting module interface.

test_steps.action: Select and generate a standard report for a specific storage area and time period (e.g., daily summary, weekly trend).
test_steps.expected_result: The system generates the selected standard report in the vendor's specified format.

test_steps.action: Review the generated report for accuracy and completeness of data, ensuring it aligns with recorded environmental conditions.
test_steps.expected_result: The report accurately reflects the recorded temperature and humidity data for the selected period and area, and is suitable for batch release review.
data_to_capture: Notes on any discrepancies or missing information.

acceptance_criteria: The EMS successfully generates standard reports as provided by the vendor.
Generated reports are accurate, complete, and in the correct format.
Reports are suitable for use in batch release decisions.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-007: Standard reports provided by vendor shall be used for batch release.
data_integrity_requirements: Reports must accurately reflect recorded data.
Reports must be generated in a format that preserves data integrity.

test_cases.test_name: Verify System Availability and Planned Maintenance Exclusion
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS meets the specified availability requirement of 99.5%, excluding periods of planned maintenance.
prerequisites: EMS has been operational for a sufficient period to gather availability data (e.g., at least one month).
Records of system downtime and planned maintenance are available.

test_steps.action: Obtain system uptime logs and records of any unplanned downtime from the EMS or system administrator.
test_steps.expected_result: Comprehensive logs detailing system operational status and downtime events are provided.
data_to_capture: Records of unplanned downtime events (dates, times, duration).

test_steps.action: Obtain records of all scheduled or planned maintenance activities that resulted in system unavailability.
test_steps.expected_result: A clear list of planned maintenance activities, including dates and durations, is provided.
data_to_capture: Records of planned maintenance (dates, times, duration).

test_steps.action: Calculate the total operational time and the total unplanned downtime for the EMS over the defined period.
test_steps.expected_result: Calculations are performed accurately, identifying total operational hours and total unplanned downtime hours.

test_steps.action: Calculate the system availability percentage using the formula: (Total Operational Time - Total Unplanned Downtime) / Total Operational Time * 100.
test_steps.expected_result: The calculated availability percentage is determined.

test_steps.action: Compare the calculated availability percentage against the URS requirement of 99.5%.
test_steps.expected_result: The calculated availability percentage meets or exceeds the 99.5% requirement.
data_to_capture: Confirmation of availability percentage meeting requirement.

acceptance_criteria: The EMS achieves a minimum availability of 99.5% over the tested period, excluding planned maintenance.
All unplanned downtime events are documented and accounted for.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-013: System availability shall be 99.5% excluding planned maintenance.
data_integrity_requirements: Accurate logging of system status is crucial for availability calculation.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Facility Management System Integration and Alarm Notification
test_cases.objective: To verify the seamless integration of the EMS with the existing facility management system and the proper functioning of alarm notifications via the site paging system.
prerequisites: EMS is installed and configured.
Facility management system is operational.
Site paging system is operational.
Vendor API for alarm notifications is accessible and configured.

test_steps.action: Simulate a temperature deviation exceeding the alarm threshold in a monitored GMP storage area.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS generates an alarm notification.

test_steps.action: Verify that the alarm notification is successfully transmitted to the site paging system via the vendor API.
test_steps.expected_result: An alert is received on the designated paging system.

test_steps.action: Verify that the EMS data is correctly reflected in the facility management system.
test_steps.expected_result: Temperature readings and alarm status from the EMS are accurately displayed within the facility management system interface.
data_to_capture: Screenshots of EMS data in facility management system
Comparison of EMS readings with facility management system display

acceptance_criteria: Alarm notifications are generated by the EMS within the specified response time.
Alarm notifications are successfully delivered to the site paging system.
EMS data is accurately integrated and displayed within the facility management system.
data_integrity_requirements: Data transmitted between systems must be accurate and complete.

test_cases.test_name: Verify System Availability and Planned Maintenance Exclusion
test_cases.objective: To confirm that the EMS meets the specified availability requirement of 99.5% and that planned maintenance activities are correctly excluded from this calculation.
prerequisites: EMS has been operational for a sufficient period to gather availability data (e.g., 1 month).
Records of all system downtime, including planned maintenance, are available.

test_steps.action: Gather all system downtime records for the defined observation period.
test_steps.expected_result: A comprehensive list of all unscheduled and scheduled downtime events is compiled.
data_to_capture: Start and end times for each downtime event
Reason for downtime (planned maintenance vs. unscheduled)

test_steps.action: Calculate the total operational time of the EMS during the observation period.
test_steps.expected_result: The total time the system was available and functioning is accurately calculated.

test_steps.action: Calculate the system availability percentage, excluding planned maintenance.
test_steps.expected_result: The calculated availability percentage meets or exceeds the 99.5% requirement.

test_steps.action: Review the documentation and records for any planned maintenance activities to ensure they were correctly identified and excluded from the availability calculation.
test_steps.expected_result: All planned maintenance activities are clearly documented and were not counted as unscheduled downtime.

acceptance_criteria: The calculated system availability, excluding planned maintenance, is >= 99.5%.
All planned maintenance activities are clearly documented and were correctly excluded from the availability calculation.
data_integrity_requirements: Downtime records must be accurate and complete.
